assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, and the policy-rule and welfare analysis built on it, underpins modern central-bank practice and most applied monetary policy research. Its influence on both theory and institutions is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is wide. Woodford (microfounded policy analysis and optimal monetary policy), Taylor (policy rules and staggered contracts) and Gali (the canonical NK model and its empirical use) are the most coherent core. Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are important but could be left out without breaking the central narrative. Leaving them out is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1980 to 2010 and has been tested through several decades of policy use, including the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation. The 2022 award on banking and crises did not cover this area. The timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee can draw a defensible three-person boundary given Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets.
Debate over how well the NK model performed during the 2021-23 inflation.
Possible overlap with earlier macro prizes (Lucas, Prescott, Sargent and Sims).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade paradigm changed how trade is theorized and measured. Selection, exporter premia and the new margins of gains from trade now drive empirical trade research and trade-policy evaluation. It built on, and went beyond, the 2008 prize for new trade theory.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear core. Helpman provides the broader theoretical architecture and the later work on firm-level trade, with Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus FDI. Redding is a strong extender, but a two-person award seems the cleanest. I am close to this field, so I am disclosing my own prior beliefs here.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of firm-level evidence across many countries confirm the central mechanisms. The paradigm is well established.
uncertainties: Whether Redding, or the Bernard-Jensen empirical line, should be included in the credit.
How the Committee weighs a second trade prize after 2008.
My own field proximity may bias my sense of this work's importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimating demand for differentiated products with endogenous prices (BLP), and the dynamic-industry framework around it, created the standard toolkit for merger analysis, antitrust and empirical IO. Its practical effect on competition policy is large.
assessment.attribution: BLP (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes 1995) is the central discovery. Pakes also developed the dynamic oligopoly framework with Ericson, and the estimation work with Olley, Benkard and others. Bresnahan and Reiss are important precursors, and Bresnahan could arguably replace one of the three. Credit is therefore reasonably focused but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use in academia, antitrust agencies and industry. Methodological critiques exist but have refined the approach rather than undermined it.
uncertainties: Bresnahan's and Reiss's precursor roles may complicate the choice of three.
Concerns about identification and reliance on functional-form assumptions.
Industrial organization is my own research area, so I am disclosing possible bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano-Bond, Arellano-Bover, Blundell-Bond) are among the most-used tools in applied microeconometrics, and have supported empirical work in growth, firm dynamics and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio matches the core estimator papers well. Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen, and Anderson-Hsiao, are antecedents that are not credited here. Blundell is also credited in B020, so his contribution would need to be placed in a single frame.
assessment.maturity: Used for more than 30 years. Well-known weak-instrument and proliferation caveats are understood.
uncertainties: Methodological tools have a mixed record of Nobel recognition relative to conceptual discoveries.
Antecedent credit (Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin et al.).
Concerns about instrument proliferation and misuse in practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore credit cycles and the financial-accelerator line explain how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. They became central to post-2008 macro-finance and are a core part of how financial frictions enter macroeconomic models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) are the conceptual core. Gertler's contributions (Bernanke-Gertler, Gertler-Kiyotaki) bridge theory and quantitative macro. Bernanke has already been recognized (2022), and Gilchrist is an empirical extender. Gertler also appears in B037, which would require care.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with a heavy policy role since 2008. The financial crisis supplied strong external validation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Gertler's overlapping credit in B037.
Boundary with Hart-Moore incomplete-contracts credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and of place-based and policy effects on opportunity. It has had large public and policy influence, and it sets new empirical standards.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the leading figure, with Hendren and Friedman as the closest collaborators on the mobility and neighbourhood work. Katz is an important contributor (Moving to Opportunity) but is a more natural fit for other lines. Team-based credit may be unwieldy.
assessment.maturity: Substantial and influential, but the work is recent, so long-run replication and follow-up on lasting policy effects are still developing.
uncertainties: Maturity: the main findings are mostly from after 2014, and long-run policy effects are not yet fully tested.
Disagreement about how causal the place-based estimates are.
How the Committee would divide credit across a large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Axiomatic models of decision-making under ambiguity (maxmin and Choquet expected utility, recursive ambiguity in dynamic settings) offer a rigorous response to Ellsberg-type behaviour and Knightian uncertainty, with applications in finance and macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: The core maxmin result is Gilboa-Schmeidler (1989). Schmeidler (Choquet expected utility) died in 2022, so he is not eligible. Epstein contributed dynamic ambiguity models, and Marinacci contributed later work. The proposed pair is defensible, but a different pairing could be argued.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature and well established. Empirical and applied validation, such as ambiguity in asset pricing, is more mixed.
uncertainties: Schmeidler's death leaves the central credit incomplete.
The empirical and applied footprint is narrower than the theoretical influence.
I have a personal interest in the Knightian-uncertainty literature and should discount any bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment reshaped understanding of trade, technology and wage inequality, and had large influence on policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both lines, and Hanson and Dorn are essential to the trade-shock work. The task framework also owes a lot to Acemoglu, Restrepo and Levy-Murnane, and Acemoglu was recognized in 2024. The credit may therefore be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with a decade-plus of replication and extensions. Debate continues on persistence and on generalization beyond the US.
uncertainties: Overlap with Acemoglu's 2024 recognition for related technology and institutions work.
Contested interpretation of the long-run labour-market effects.
Whether this is better seen as a major empirical contribution than as a conceptual discovery.
